day_1.utterance: Come on! Let's get everything useful over here — move it!
day_1.response: Yeah yeah I'm moving, give me a second. What are we actually looking for here, food and water first or...?

day_1.utterance: I thought we were going to die. Did you get that feeling… like your mind just went completely blank?
day_1.response: Yeah honestly yeah. It's like your brain just stops working for a second. Are you hurt though? Can you move?

day_1.utterance: *Sits silently against the wreckage, staring into the distance, not moving, not saying a word.*
day_1.response: Hey. Hey, look at me. I get it, I really do, but sitting here isn't gonna help either of us. I need you to get up.

day_1.utterance: First-aid kit is good for three days. Two bottles of water. Food is basically nothing.
day_1.response: Okay so water is the priority then. Food we can maybe figure out but we need more water asap. What else did you find, any containers we could use to collect rainwater or anything?

day_1.utterance: Inventory's done. Priorities in order: water, shelter, signal.
day_1.response: Okay yeah I agree with that order. Where are we even, like is there any chance there's a river or stream nearby? I feel like we should send someone to scout while the rest of us set up some kind of shelter situation.

day_1.utterance: So — how do we split the blankets?
day_1.response: Two blankets, four people. I mean someone's sharing, it's not that complicated. Michelangelo and I can take one, you two figure out the other. Or we all just crowd around the fire and call it good enough for tonight.

day_2.utterance: Freshwater source is to the northeast — two hours on foot. Someone has to go tomorrow. You or DaVinci?
day_2.response: I'll go. DaVinci can hold things down here and make sure Michelangelo is okay. Two hours isn't bad. What am I looking for exactly, like landmarks or anything so I don't get completely turned around out there?

day_2.utterance: Today's tasks: collect fresh water, patch the weak spots in camp, sort the first-aid kit. I'll handle the water. You and DaVinci split the other two.
day_2.response: Wait, I thought I was going just said I'd go. Are you changing the plan or did you not hear me? I'm fine either way but let's just pick one and stick to it, no point in both of us heading out there.

day_2.utterance: I… I can't find my stuff. The gauze from the first-aid kit — have you seen it?
day_2.response: No I haven't seen it, did you check where Donatello had the kit set up? Actually wait, speaking of Donatello — did you put that empty bottle next to the rationing plan on purpose? Because I saw that and I'm not gonna pretend I didn't. We need to talk about that.

day_2.utterance: Before Donatello came back just now… I saw her put a pack of crackers into her own bag. What do you think we should do?
day_2.response: Okay so that's twice now. I'm not gonna sit here and pretend everything's fine, that's not fair to the rest of us. We need to say something to her directly, not leave bottles around or hint at it. I get that it's uncomfortable but if she's hoarding food and water we're all screwed. I'll bring it up. You don't have to say anything if you don't want to but I'm not letting this go.

day_2.utterance: Hey… any chance the camp repairs can wait until tomorrow? We've already done a lot today.
day_2.response: I mean yeah probably, but I wanna deal with the Donatello thing first before we all go to sleep and pretend it didn't happen. That's more important than the repairs honestly.

day_2.utterance: Hey — that knot I tied should be holding, right?
day_2.response: Food storage. Sorry Michelangelo, you can move closer to the middle but if the food gets wet we're all in a worse situation than one person being uncomfortable tonight.

day_2.utterance: A leak over the food storage has worse consequences. But it's your call.
day_2.response: Yeah we already made the call, food storage. Let's just do it, you don't need to validate it Donatello.
Don't apologize, it's fine. You okay?

day_3.utterance: You think it's a waste of time?
day_3.response: No I think it's actually one of the smarter things we've done. Like what else are we supposed to do, just not try? Keep the flowers.

day_3.utterance: I've written up the raft plan — take a look. We'd use the metal panels and straps from the wreckage. Two days to build. There's a risk of capsizing. Do you think it's workable?
day_3.response: I mean it could work. Two days is doable. The capsizing thing is the part that worries me though, like what's the actual risk there, are we talking rough water or is it more a structural issue with the panels? Because if it's structural maybe we can reinforce it somehow. I don't wanna shoot it down but I also don't wanna build a raft for two days and then flip it twenty feet from shore.

day_3.utterance: I didn't sleep last night. I kept thinking — if rescue never comes, what kind of people do you think we'll end up becoming?
day_3.response: Honestly I think about that too. Like I'd like to think I'd stay the same but then you see stuff like Donatello with the crackers and it's like... maybe not everyone does. I think you just have to decide early who you wanna be and stick to it. That's all you can do.

day_3.utterance: *Walks a little way from camp and sits down alone, back to everyone, not saying anything.*
What do you usually do when you're not busy?
day_3.response: Honestly? Probably vaping and going down rabbit holes online until 3am. Not exactly survival skills. You?

day_3.utterance: I'll tell you something, but don't tell the others. I can swim. That reef out there is maybe five hundred meters — I've been thinking about swimming out tomorrow to signal from there.
day_3.response: Okay but why are we keeping that secret from the others? Like I'm not gonna stop you but if something goes wrong out there and nobody knows where you are that's a problem. Tell Donatello at least, she'd want to know for practical reasons if nothing else.

day_3.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal pile. It hasn't been touched.
day_3.response: Yeah I know, I got sidetracked. I'll go do it now. Also heads up, DaVinci has something to tell you before tomorrow morning, just make sure you actually listen to the whole thing before you start poking holes in it.

Kinda yeah? Like I get that you're tracking resources and tasks but logging where everyone was and what they were doing without telling anyone feels a little... I dunno, surveillance-y. What's the point of it exactly.

day_3.utterance: *Keeps her head down, writing in her notebook throughout, never joining in — as if none of this concerns her.*
day_3.response: Still feels weird. Like even if your intentions are fine, maybe just mention it to people? "Hey I'm keeping a log" is not a hard thing to say.

day_3.utterance: I just thought of something — if we pull off one of the plane's mirror panels and angle it toward the sun, the reflection could reach really far. Way more visible than an SOS.
day_3.response: Oh that's actually a really good idea. Way better than anything I came up with. Do you know how to angle it properly or is it kind of just trial and error?

day_3.utterance: There's something I've been keeping to myself. If I don't say it here, I might never get the chance.
day_3.response: Okay now I'm nervous. What is it?

day_3.utterance: I took piano lessons when I was a kid… three years, then I just stopped practicing. Is there anything you're really into — music, books, drawing, anything like that?
day_3.response: I used to be really into music yeah, like I'd spend hours just finding new stuff and making playlists. Never learned an instrument though. Why'd you stop with the piano? Three years is actually a decent amount of time, you probably still remember more than you think.

day_3.utterance: The frame of the raft has to be finished today — otherwise we can't start lashing it together tomorrow. I know everyone's tired, but stopping now means one more day.
day_3.response: Yeah I know, I know. Let's just get it done then. Michelangelo, you good to help? The sooner we finish the sooner we can actually stop for the night.

day_4.utterance: I… I want to say something, but… never mind.
day_4.response: No, say it. What is it.

day_4.utterance: *The smile freezes on his face. He can't keep it up. He quietly sits down and buries his face in his hands.*
day_4.response: It wasn't the last chance. It can't be. We have the mirror panel, we have the SOS on the beach, DaVinci's still got the reef idea. That plane means there are planes. That's actually something.

day_4.utterance: I was going to get supplies… wait, what's that over there?
day_4.response: Where? What are you looking at?

day_4.utterance: You said you were going to check the signal equipment. So where did you go?
day_4.response: I went to sit with Michelangelo for a bit, we needed a minute. The signal stuff is on my list, I'll go do it right now. Relax.

day_4.utterance: There's something I never told you all. Before we left, I told my family our flight path. They know roughly where we were headed. I just don't know if they'll call it in.
day_4.response: Wait, seriously? Why didn't you say this sooner, that's actually huge. Like if they know the flight path and we've been missing long enough they've definitely called it in by now. That's not a small thing Michelangelo, that's probably the best news we've had since we got here.

day_4.utterance: If the information is accurate, rescue could arrive within 48 hours. We need to keep our current supplies intact until then.
day_4.response: Okay so then we don't touch anything. 48 hours is nothing, we can do 48 hours. Someone should probably feed the fire though so they can actually see us when they get here.

day_4.utterance: Are you scared? …I am. Not of dying. I'm scared of just… disappearing without leaving anything behind.
day_4.response: Yeah. I think about that too honestly. Like not even in a dramatic way, just... you want to matter to someone. Leave some kind of mark. I don't think you're disappearing though. I'm gonna remember you after this, for whatever that's worth.

day_5.utterance: *Stands up, eyes red, looking at you and the others. His lips move, but nothing comes out.*
day_5.response: Hey. Hey, we're okay. We're actually okay.

day_5.utterance: These past few days… I know I haven't been easy to be around.
day_5.response: No you haven't, but you kept us alive so. I'll take it.

day_5.utterance: *The three of them drift apart, each doing their own thing. No one takes charge. The silence settles over the camp.*
day_5.response: Alright I'm not just gonna sit here for three hours. Let's at least make this place look like we weren't completely feral while we were here.

day_5.utterance: I dreamed about home last night.
day_5.response: What was it like? Good dream or one of those ones where you're home but something's still off?
I know. And I'm not gonna make a big thing out of it right now, not with rescue three hours away. But you know it wasn't okay, right?

day_5.utterance: I logged every resource and decision from these five days. I'm going to write it up as a proper report when we get back. On the last page I left myself a question I haven't answered yet — if you had to do it over, what would you change?
day_5.response: Honestly? I'd have called out the food thing sooner instead of waiting for it to pile up. I let it go too long because I didn't want the conflict and that wasn't fair to anyone. What would you change?

day_5.utterance: First thing when I get back — I'm going to compile all the resource data from these five days into a report.
day_5.response: Yeah that tracks for you. Send me a copy when you're done, I'm genuinely curious what it looks like all written out.

day_5.utterance: Those flowers DaVinci drew on the beach… I never really understood what they were for. What practical purpose did they serve out here?
day_5.response: Nothing practical. That's kind of the whole point.

day_5.utterance: *His cheering stops. He looks over at you, notices you haven't moved, and the smile slowly fades. He waits.*
day_5.response: I'm coming, I just need a second.

day_5.utterance: Rescue is here… they're waving us over. Are you going? I'll follow you.
